test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What name did ancient Chinese texts use for India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Yintu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In ancient **Chinese** literature, the term **Yintu** (also written as **Yin-tu** or **Yindu**) was used to refer to the Indian subcontinent. ***Hence, option 3 is correct.***
 
• The name **Yintu** is a phonetic transliteration of the **Sanskrit** word **Sindhu**, which is the name of the river **Indus**.
 
• The famous **Chinese** Buddhist monk and scholar **Xuanzang** (Hsuan-tsang), who visited **India** during the **7th century AD** (specifically between **629 AD** and **645 AD**), standardized this name in his writings.
 
• Before **Xuanzang**, various other names were found in **Chinese** records, such as **Shendu** (used during the **Han Dynasty**) and **Tiandu**, all of which were early attempts to capture the sound of **Sindhu**.
 
• **Xuanzang** noted that the name **Yintu** was more accurate than previous versions to describe the vast land located to the west of **China**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bharat**:

 
 
• It is the indigenous and constitutional name of **India**.
 
• The name is derived from the ancient **Bharata** tribe or the legendary **King Bharata**, a descendant of the **Puru** dynasty.
 
• It is mentioned in ancient **Sanskrit** texts like the **Rigveda** and the **Puranas**, where **Bharatavarsha** refers to the geographical entity of the subcontinent.
 
 
 
• **Indica**:
 
 
• This is the title of a historical account written by **Megasthenes**, a **Greek** ethnographer and ambassador.
 
• He was sent to the court of **Chandragupta Maurya** around **300 BC** by the **Hellenistic** king **Seleucus I Nicator**.
 
• The book provides vital information about the **Mauryan** administration, social classes, and the city of **Pataliputra**.
 
 
 
• **Sindhu**:
 
 
• This is the **Sanskrit** name for the **Indus River**, one of the longest rivers in **Asia**.
 
• The **Persians**, who had difficulty pronouncing 'S', called the river **Hindu** and the land **Hindustan**.
 
• The **Greeks** later dropped the 'H' to call the river **Indos**, which eventually led to the **Latin** name **India**.
 
 
 
• **Tianzhu**:
 
 
• This was another historical **Chinese** name for **India**, especially used during the **Han Dynasty**.
 
• The term translates to "**Heavenly Center**," reflecting the high regard **Chinese** Buddhists had for **India** as the birthplace of **Lord Buddha**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Xuanzang's** travelogue, **"Great Tang Records on the Western Regions"**, is a primary source for the history of **India** during the reign of **King Harshavardhana**.
 
• Cultural and religious exchanges between **India** and **China** were primarily facilitated through the **Silk Road**, leading to the spread of **Buddhism** in **China**.
 
• The modern **Chinese** word for **India** is **Yindu**, which is a direct phonetic descendant of the ancient **Yintu**.
 
• The diverse names for **India** across different civilizations (**Hindustan**, **India**, **Yintu**) all share a common etymological root in the **Sindhu** (Indus) river.
